script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination 2026. English Language Paper 3. Listening and Integrated Skills.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: The entire broadcast will last approximately one hour. During the examination, you will hear several recordings. You will have time to read the instructions and the questions. You will also have time to check your work.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Part A. Task 1. You are at the check-in counter for the Future Tourism Expo. You will hear a conversation between a staff member and an exhibitor. Complete the registration form below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Good morning! Welcome to the Future Tourism Expo 2026. We are expecting a huge crowd today—nearly four thousand attendees. How can I help you with your registration today?

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Hello! I'm here to confirm the booth details for Wilderness Retreats Ltd. My name is Marcus Thorpe. Have you got us on your list?

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Let me see... Wilderness Retreats... Ah, yes, here it is. Marcus Thorpe, m.thorpe@wilderness.com.hk. Your booth category is Eco-Glamping Pavilion on Hall 3C.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: That's correct. We're displaying 3 tents and need 8 tablets for our interactive booking demo. We also require a 220V high voltage connection for our climate-control display.

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Three tents, eight tablets, 220V high voltage. Noted. Your media interview slot is Friday at 2:00 PM. Insurance policy WR-9988-X is valid. I see you received the 15% early bird discount.

script.speaker: Marcus
script.text: Yes, the 15% discount. And my biometric entry code?

script.speaker: Staff
script.text: Your code is ECO-2026-GL. You're all set, Mr. Thorpe. Enjoy the expo!

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 2. You will hear a podcast episode regarding 'The Glamping Boom in the New Territories'. Listen to the podcast and complete the notes below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Welcome to 'Travel HK' podcast. Today we're discussing the glamping boom. We currently have 42 registered sites across the New Territories. Yuen Long has overtaken Sai Kung as the most popular district.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: The average nightly rate is 1,800 dollars. Young families are the primary demographic. But waste management is the biggest challenge for operators. Autumn sees the highest booking rate due to the perfect weather.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Legally, operators need a Short Term Tenancy permit and a Fire Safety Type B certificate. Guests come mainly for the star-gazing experience. The next project is in Lantau South. Annual growth is estimated at 22%. Our key collaborator is the Eco-Travel Association.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 3. You will hear three experts debating 'Traditional Hotels vs. Glamping'. Listen to the discussion and tick the correct boxes in the table. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Moderator
script.text: Welcome to our hospitality panel. Joining us are Prof. Ng, Mr. Lau, and Ms. Cheung. Prof. Ng, what's your view on hotel heritage?

script.speaker: Prof Ng
script.text: For a world-class city like Hong Kong, our heritage hotels are indispensable. Traditional hotel occupancy is still respectable at 68%.

script.speaker: Mr Lau
script.text: But people are tired of concrete boxes. The main concern with hotels is the lack of nature. Glamping occupancy is at 85%! I'm pushing for a 500 million dollar subsidy for eco-tourism.

script.speaker: Ms Cheung
script.text: Why not a hybrid model? Hotels could install tented villas. We should set a minimum guest age of 6 for safety and a noise limit of 55 decibels. Hotels should get EarthCheck Gold certification.

script.speaker: Moderator
script.text: What about revenue sources?

script.speaker: Prof Ng
script.text: Hotels rely on business travelers.

script.speaker: Mr Lau
script.text: Glamping thrives on leisure weekends. Let's meet again on August 12 to finalise standards.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 4. You will hear three stakeholders discussing the regulation of 'Wild Camping' in the New Territories. Listen to their conversation and complete the matrix below. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Today we're joined by an Environmentalist, a Local Resident, and a Tour Operator. Let's discuss wild camping regulation. Environmentalist, what's your concern?

script.speaker: Environmentalist
script.text: We're seeing severe soil erosion in protected zones. The 2025 Biodiversity Audit proved the damage. We need drone patrols on weekends.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: And the trash! I'm tired of cleaning up after tourists. We want a 3,000 dollar fine for littering and permit-only parking for villagers.

script.speaker: Operator
script.text: I suggest a digital permit system to limit group sizes to 8 people. We're happy to carry third-party indemnity insurance.

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Can we agree on next steps?

script.speaker: Environmentalist
script.text: Let's move to the public consultation phase.

script.speaker: Resident
script.text: Target implementation by January 2027.

script.speaker: Operator
script.text: And the official hotline should be 1823-CAMP.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (60-second pause to tidy up answers)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: That is the end of Part A. You now have five minutes to study the Part B Question-Answer Book and the Data File. (300-second pause)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Integrated Skills Recording. You will now hear a briefing from the Director of the Staycation Bureau, Janice Wong, to the Project Manager regarding the upcoming tasks. Listen carefully and take notes as you will need this information to complete the tasks in Part B.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: Good morning. I'm glad we're finally getting started on these tasks. We have a lot to do before the Q4 rollout. When you write that letter to the Village Residents' Association for Task 8, please don't just repeat the brochure points. Emphasise that we aren't just creating 'tourism' jobs for hotel staff. Mention that we are specifically looking to hire people with 'ecological expertise' and 'village liaison experience' to bridge the gap between glamping development and rural communities. That's a key detail not in the Data File yet.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: Moving on to the internal memo for Task 9—don't just list the budget gap. Propose a specific 'Green Getaway Week' in December to fix the publicity issue. We need to get local travel influencers involved to build trust. And for the public social media post in Task 10, make sure to use a friendly, non-corporate tone. Use the phrase 'Wild Luxury, Local Heart' and make it sound like a neighbour talking to a neighbour.

script.speaker: Janice
script.text: One last thing—I just heard from the Environmental Protection Department. They are very insistent that we describe our waste composting system as 'Zero Trace'. That's the specific term they want us to use in our responses to citizens like Ms. Gladys Ho. 'Zero Trace'. Got it? Good. I expect those drafts on my desk by the end of the day. Good luck.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: That is the end of the Integrated Skills recording. You now have 1 hour and 10 minutes to complete your tasks. Stop writing when you hear the signal at the end of the examination.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: (4200-second pause)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Stop writing now. The examination is over. Please stay in your seats until your scripts have been collected.

data_file.title: Minutes of the Rural Tourism Development Meeting
data_file.content:
Date: May 12, 2026. Attendees: Director Lo, PM Sarah Ho.
Discussion: Residents in Yuen Long complained about light pollution from glamping sites.
Action: Proposal for 'Dark Sky' compliance certification for all new sites.
Note: Need to highlight that eco-tourism creates long-term village employment (Doc 9).

data_file.title: Starry Nights Glamping: Guest Guide
data_file.content: Experience the NT like never before. 100% solar powered. Nightly stargazing tours. No loud music after 10 PM. All trash must be carried out. Complimentary telescopes provided.

data_file.title: Email from Ms. Gladys Ho (Resident)
data_file.content:
To: Staycation Bureau Feedback
Subject: Light and Noise Complaints

I live in Kam Tin and the new glamping site is like a stadium at night. My children can't sleep. The floodlights are pointed right at our village. And the tourists leave trash everywhere. Please act immediately or I will organise a village protest.

data_file.title: Editorial: Hotels vs. Tents—The Battle for Tourist Dollars
data_file.content: HK Daily News: Traditional hotels in urban areas are struggling with 60% occupancy, while NT glamping sites are fully booked at 85%. Experts suggest hotels must 'go green' or risk losing the leisure market entirely.

data_file.title: Urgent Note from Director Janice Wong (Post-it Note)
data_file.content:
To: Project Manager

Just saw Gladys Ho's email (Doc 3). We MUST reply to her. Be firm but polite. Explain that 'Dark Sky' compliance is mandatory from next month. Also, mention the waste composting system. We can't afford a village protest right now. Also, for the internal memo (Task 9), make sure you mention we are hiring 80 'Eco-Guides' to show we are creating jobs!

data_file.title: Table 1: Staycation Voucher Performance (Q1 2026)
data_file.content:
District | Vouchers Issued | Vouchers Redeemed
Sai Kung | 5,000 | 4,800
Yuen Long | 4,000 | 1,200 (CRITICALLY LOW!)
Lantau | 3,000 | 2,500

Note: The low uptake in Yuen Long is directly linked to resident complaints about light and noise.

data_file.title: Viral Post from 'Save Our Greenery' NGO
data_file.content: Glamping is just 'gentrified destruction'. They are trampling the rare orchids and scaring fireflies. #SaveOurNT #NatureFirst

data_file.title: Internal Memo: Licensing Update
data_file.content: To all staff: New regulation requires all glamping sites to maintain a 1:10 staff-to-guest ratio. All sites must provide eco-friendly toiletries. Waste must be sorted into four categories.

data_file.title: Research: Eco-Tourism Employment Impact
data_file.content: A recent university study found that eco-tourism sites create 3.2 local jobs per hectare, compared to 0.8 for traditional agriculture. Villages with glamping sites saw a 15% increase in youth retention.

data_file.title: Draft Section: Dark Sky Compliance
data_file.content: Clause 6.1: All outdoor lighting in designated rural tourism zones must be downward-facing and shielded. Maximum lux level at property boundary: 5. Non-compliant sites face suspension of operating licence.
